- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile.  
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., > -0.50) — model tends to ignore bearish sentiment.  
- Overshoot early in forecast horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — model reacts too aggressively.  
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after recent peaks, especially if sentiment is weak or mixed.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price by 5–10% to account for downward pressure.  
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings — model often overcorrects in direction, ignoring longer-term trend.  
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling, model tends to underestimate the drop — adjust downward by 2–5% for such cases.
